answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to hold a small time-locked stake that only matures through verifiable work, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs real capital and time. Like a zephyr slipping through a narrow inlet yet unable to shift shale, cheap identities pass surface checks but stall at the stake: reputation accrues slowly from attested tasks, and one misbehavior slashes the deposit. Newcomers earn wider access only as their record grows, making mass fakery expensive while honest agents compound trust.
